# Independent audit of frozen vertical projective cuts

Source read in full: `candidate 0461931dd06b8049`. Verdict: **PASS**. No mathematical repair is required. The companion exact verifier was independently rerun: **13,552 checks PASS**.

The actual finite-plane body is positive and bounded for both signs of small t: the continuous facet normals have no common nonzero recession direction, their uniform positive-spanning bound persists, and the finitely many sampled interior balls retain strict slack. The projection remains exactly the old base polytope. Canonical replacement preserves every sampled fiber, without an unproved claim about real-base sections.

The radial active-constraint calculation gives the maximum of the signed values B_r ell with no additional zero. For negative t it gives the maximum of -B_r ell; these are negatives only if the old active coefficients agree or ell vanishes. The printed absolute-value range identity is correct, including either sign of ell and intercepts of either sign. The interval crease example indeed has speeds 4 and -2 at each endpoint.

For a fixed measured normal, an ambient support plane active at a convex combination of boundary points must be active at every positive input: its affine nonnegative slack has average zero. This proves the Jensen restriction for both speed choices. Subdivision into finitely many affine cells then makes the lower convex roof of the marked cell vertices agree on the entire same-normal measured set. Its finitely many lower affine pieces supply a globally finite convex extension, also in a deficient affine span. Continuous nonnegative normal selectors interpolate the finitely many measured normal directions. Thus the claimed speed belongs exactly to the old signed normal-dependent convex cone, not merely to its closure.

For a compact complete support menu, the penalty maximum decreases to the active maximum on the old normal bundle. Completeness supplies an active index and hence a uniform lower bound even for signed fields; the nonnegative old slack supplies the upper bound. This justifies dominated convergence for every bounded stress pairing. It does not turn the two signs into an odd derivative.

The prism affine change sends the two endpoints exactly to plus/minus(1-ta z). Its determinant is common to all fibers and cap masses. The all-slope middle depth is 3-2|ta| and dominates the endpoint maxima precisely in the stated range |ta|<2/3. Therefore beta_t=1/2-|ta|/3 is exact. When a=0 the path is an actual common affine image, explaining the cancellation of all normalized higher-order terms in that example. The final product/projective identity is also exact while its denominator remains positive.

The conclusion is correctly limited: the construction is a legal fixed-lattice deformation, but its first speeds add no constraint to the established normal-convex stress. The source does not dismiss second-order information for general non-product bodies.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
